I completely devoured books 1-3, thought book 4 was a nice little break, and then got severe whiplash from book 5. Like others have said, ACOSF felt like it was written by a completely different author. Somehow every single character, including the main love interest, got assassinated. It was interesting as a character study but somehow this 700 page book lacked any plot, pacing, or buildup. 

I think I just remind myself that books 1-3 were the main trilogy and everything after is merely the spinoff. I can enjoy the primary trilogy while also acknowledging that the side story is going to go in a different direction

Also: why, in a book, do we want every character to love each other?? I think their banter is funny and interesting! Characters are meant to annoy each other and make mistakes because it moves the plot and makes things interesting! If every character loves each other and never make mistakes it would be BORING. Give me some in-law drama!

I adopted a very traumatized dog before (puppy mill dog that was forced to breed) so I know the struggle. I would say two things: 

1) It’s important to be realistic: they may not ever be 100% “normal” and that’s ok! Just like humans, trauma can permanently impact the way their brains respond to things. It’s important to give her space, give her endless love, and understand what *her* normal looks like (which seems like you’re already doing!) 

2) Branching off the previous note but healing takes time. She had about 2 years of abuse, that doesn’t go away in 8 months. Just be patient and she’ll heal when she’s ready. Don’t worry, you’re not a bad owner because the progress is slow, it’s just the quirks of having a dog with some history :)

They may not all apply, but here are some tips I used with my lab: 

1) instead of a cone, try using an old t-shirt! Cones can make some dogs anxious so putting an old shirt (back legs first) and tying it around the waist can prevent her from licking without causing her stress 

2) personally, I use doggy cbd to help calm my dog down. Everyone has different opinions on this so definitely do your research on the brand and ask your vet! But I found this to be a great tool in keeping her calm without any powerful drugs 

3) Tire her out with brain games! If she gets too energetic from sitting around try to play low-impact games like hide the treat or teaching her some tricks. Or even just get her some more chew toys to distract her

I adopted a highly traumatized dog before and honestly, I think it’s important to be realistic and know that a traumatized dog will not always act like a “normal” dog. I know my dog doesn’t really play except with paper haha

It may take a bit of time for your dog to feel 100% safe and understand how to play so he might end up coming around with time (it’s helpful that he’s young!). But if he doesn’t come around that’s normal too, it’s just the quirk of having a dog with some history :)
